items.headline: Users may be unable to access or perform several actions in Microsoft 365 services
items.summary: User impact: Users may have been unable to access or perform several actions in Microsoft 365 services. Final status: We've confirmed that the services across the previously affected environments have fully recovered and the backlog of email messages has been processed, thus this issue is remediated. Start time: Thursday, November 12, 2026, at 10:05 AM UTC End time: Friday, November 13, 2026, at 4:10 PM UTC This is the final update for the event.
lines: Users may have been unable to access or perform several actions in Microsoft 365 services.
The issue started November 12, 2026, at 10:05 AM UTC and ended November 13, 2026, at 4:10 PM UTC.
Microsoft confirmed that services in the previously affected environments have fully recovered and the email backlog has been processed.

lines: Google Cloud announced expanded AI agent observability and evaluation capabilities across Google Data Cloud.

items.headline: Aurora PostgreSQL with express configuration now supported in CloudFormation
items.summary: Aurora PostgreSQL now supports express configuration in AWS CloudFormation for infrastructure as code deployment. This launch enables you to automate the infrastructure deployment of your Aurora clusters through CloudFormation templates while benefiting from the speed of express configuration. Aurora PostgreSQL clusters created with express configuration allow you to create and query an Aurora serverless database in seconds. The new withExpressConfiguration createOnly property on the AWS::RDS::DBCluster resource creates both the cluster and its primary database instance from one property declaration. You don't need to model or manage the instance separately in your CloudFormation template. T
lines: Aurora PostgreSQL now supports express configuration in AWS CloudFormation.
The new withExpressConfiguration createOnly property on the AWS::RDS::DBCluster resource creates the cluster and its primary database instance from one property declaration.
Teams using infrastructure as code do not need to model or manage the instance separately in their templates.

items.headline: AWS Security Hub CSPM now supports centralized configuration with AWS Organizations declarative policies
items.summary: AWS Security Hub CSPM now supports AWS Organizations declarative policies. You can use them to enable Security Hub CSPM across all accounts and Regions in your organization and to define which security standards and controls are enabled. Policies can apply broadly to every account and Region, or target specific account and Region combinations. Declarative policies help keep each account's configuration aligned with its attached policy, which helps prevent configuration drift. You can also apply them automatically to new accounts, so each account starts with a baseline configuration as soon as it's created. lines: AWS Security Hub CSPM now supports AWS Organizations declarative policies.

Policies can apply automatically to new accounts and help keep each account's configuration aligned with its attached policy.

items.headline: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity now supports OAuth 2.0 discovery URLs
items.summary: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity now supports OAuth 2.0 authorization server discovery URLs for both inbound JWT authorization and outbound OAuth credential providers. This update enables developers to configure AgentCore with OAuth 2.0 authorization servers that do not use OpenID Connect (OIDC). Previously, AgentCore Identity accepted only OIDC discovery URLs. Authorization servers that implement OAuth 2.0 without OIDC publish their metadata at a different well-known path and could not be used with AgentCore. With this launch, you can use either OIDC or OAuth 2.0 authorization server discovery URLs when you configure a JWT authorizer or a custom OAuth credential provider on AgentCore. This
lines: Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Identity now supports OAuth 2.0 authorization server discovery URLs for inbound JWT authorization and outbound OAuth credential providers.
Previously, AgentCore Identity accepted only OIDC discovery URLs.
Authorization servers that implement OAuth 2.0 without OIDC can now be used with AgentCore.

items.headline: AWS Secrets Manager now supports cross-account replication
items.summary: AWS Secrets Manager now supports cross-account replication, enabling you to maintain a synchronized copy of a primary secret in a secondary AWS account for cross-account access, backup, and disaster recovery. Cross-account replication extends the existing multi-Region replication capability across account boundaries. With cross-account replication, platform or security teams can own and rotate a secret centrally, and each consuming account gets a local, always-current copy without any shared KMS keys or cross-account secret policies. The replica secret is a full, independent resource, encrypted with a customer managed KMS key owned by the replica account. Secrets Manager updates it automatic
lines: AWS Secrets Manager now supports cross-account replication of a primary secret into a secondary AWS account.
The replica is a full, independent resource encrypted with a customer managed KMS key owned by the replica account, with no shared KMS keys or cross-account secret policies required.
Platform or security teams can rotate a secret centrally while each consuming account keeps a local, current copy.
